'''AD 1''' or '''1 CE''' was the [[Epoch (reference date)|epoch year]] for the [[Anno Domini]] (AD) Christian [[calendar era]] and also the 1st year of the [[Common Era]] (CE) and the [[1st millennium]] and of the [[1st century]] of the Christian and the common era. It was a [[common year starting on Saturday]] or [[Common year starting on Sunday|Sunday]],<ref group="note">Sources disagree regarding the starting day of Julian year Anno Domino I (see [[Julian calendar#Leap year error|leap year error]] for further information).</ref> a [[common year starting on Saturday]] by the [[proleptic Julian calendar]], and a [[common year starting on Monday]] by the [[proleptic Gregorian calendar]]. In the [[Roman Empire]], AD 1 was known as the '''Year of the Consulship of Caesar and Paullus''', named after [[Roman consul]]s [[Gaius Caesar]] and [[Lucius Aemilius Paullus (consul 1)|Lucius Aemilius Paullus]], and less frequently, as year '''AUC 754''' (see ''[[ab urbe condita]]'') within the [[Roman Empire]]. The denomination "AD 1" for this year has been in consistent use since the mid-[[Middle Ages|medieval period]] when the Anno Domini (AD) calendar era became the prevalent method in Europe for naming years. It was the beginning of the [[Anno Domini|Christian era]]/[[Common Era|common era]]. The preceding year is [[1 BC]]; there is no [[Year zero|year 0]] in this numbering scheme. The ''Anno Domini'' dating system was devised in [[AD 525]] by [[Dionysius Exiguus]].

The [[Julian calendar]], a [[45 BC]] reform of the [[Roman calendar]], was the calendar used by Rome in AD 1.

== Events ==

=== By place ===

==== Roman Empire ====
* [[Tiberius]], under order of Emperor [[Augustus]], quells revolts in [[Germania]] (AD 1–[[AD 5|5]]).<ref>[[Velleius|Velleius Paterculus]], [https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Velleius_Paterculus/2D*.html#ref:Langobardi The Roman History], Book II. p 271.</ref>

==== Asia ====
* [[Confucius]] is given his first royal title ([[posthumous name]]) of Baocheng Xuan Ni Gong.<ref>Thomas A. Wilson, ''in'' Xinzhong Yao (Ed.), ''RoutledgeCurzon Encyclopedia of Confucianism'', entry "Baocheng Xuan Ni Gong", 2003, p. 26.</ref><ref>''Book of Han'', 12.351</ref>

=== By topic ===

==== Religion ====
* Birth of [[Jesus]], as assigned by [[Dionysius Exiguus]] in his [[anno Domini]] era according to at least one scholar.{{sfn|Declercq|2000}}{{sfn|Declercq|2002}} However, most scholars think that Dionysius placed the birth of Jesus in the previous year, [[1 BC]].{{sfn|Declercq|2000}}{{sfn|Declercq|2002}} Furthermore, most modern scholars do not consider Dionysius' calculations authoritative, placing the event several years earlier (see [[Chronology of Jesus]]).{{sfn|Dunn|2003}}

== Births ==
* [[Sextus Afranius Burrus]], Roman [[praetorian prefect]] (d. [[AD 62]])
* [[Izates II]], King of [[Adiabene]] (d. AD [[AD 54|54]])

== Deaths ==
* [[Amanishakheto]], queen of [[Kingdom of Kush|Kush]] ([[Nubia]])
